messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx and GRPC stream errors observed for inference-prod in az1a. Scope: ~18% error rate across serving tier, increased latency for short requests. Auto-escalation to on-call.

kai (oncall): I'm on it. Kicking off quick triage. Which routes are impacted?

jordan-sre: seeing errors on /v1/generate and /v1/stream from our edge metrics. Proxy ELB health checks show growing 502s, and host net queue latency is high on az1a instances.

ben-ml: Model pods show kv-cache misses spike, but the CPU on inference hosts is fine. Network TX queue length is elevated on several ephemeral hosts.

sam-platform: I'm pulling instance-level metrics now. aws.ec2.az1a: eni_tx_queue and ENI descriptor queuebacks up. Also ENI attach rate is normal. Looks like host NIC tx scheduling backlog causing packet drops to the proxy.

kai (oncall): Can we route a subset of traffic to eu-west1 as emergency fallback? We have capacity there. Need to assess customer impact first.

ops-bot: Pager duty action: oncall=kai, severity=sev2, incident_id=INC-2765439999.

jordan-sre: Quick mitigation plan: 1) enable cross-AZ fallback at load balancer for inference-prod (route ~25% traffic to eu-west1) 2) drain most impacted ephemerals in az1a 3) increase prefix caching TTL where safe 4) monitor error rate.

ben-ml: If we shift 25% traffic we'll see increased cost but should reduce SLO violations. Also prepare to failover model variant (smaller kv cache) if KV pressure persists.

sam-platform: Running: `aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:... --default-actions '[{"Type":"forward","TargetGroupArn":"tg-eu-west1"}]'` will take effect in ~30s. I'll only move a portion via weight changes.

kai (oncall): Do it. Marking to track. Also, Jordan, start draining affected pods with low disruption: `kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`.

jordan-sre: Copy. Draining nodes n-az1a-04 and n-az1a-07. Pod restart shows slow reconnects on gRPC streams though; connection retries spike in proxy logs. Attaching snippet: ```proxy.log: 2026-03-17T10:23:41Z grpc: error reading from stream: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing```

ben-ml: KV cache warmup after restart is costing ~30ms per request for some flows; combined with queue jitter that pushes tail latency > 400ms, causing client-side timeouts.

lia-cs: Customer impact: CS dashboard flags 8 customers with increased 5xx in last 15m, mostly low-volume API keys. Preparing templated comms for customers with SLA exposure.

sam-platform: Weight shift in ALB applied: az1a weight -> 75% to az1a, 25% to eu-west1. Error rate dropped to 11% in 2 minutes. Latency median improved slightly.

kai (oncall): Good. Keep incremental shifts. Any signs of underlying host recovery?

jordan-sre: Host-level TX queue drains slowly. We suspect kernel dql/pacing/tc qdisc issue combined with bursty egress. We're enabling per-node egress shaping mitigation to smooth bursts: applying `tc qdisc replace dev eth0 root fq_codel`. Rolling to 10 nodes as test.

ben-ml: After shaping on 5 nodes, observed reduced packet retries and 502s for those nodes. Global error rate now 6.8%. Continuing roll.

ops-bot: Note: autoscaler attempted to spawn additional G5 ephemerals in az1a but capacity allocation delayed by AWS due to AZ quota. Launch queue shows pending instance claims ~+7 minutes.

sam-platform: Confirmed. We hit AZ capacity soft-limit in az1a for our instance type. Submitted request to AZ capacity pool but ETA unknown. Fallback to other regions still best temporary path.

kai (oncall): Given pending capacity, continue fallback at 25-35% until we see stable <1% errors for 10m. Lia, please draft customer note explaining transient network impairment in az1a and actions taken. Flag any customers exceeding error SLA.

lia-cs: Draft ready in #customer-comms. Short note: "We observed network-related errors affecting inference requests in a single AWS availability zone. We've shifted traffic and implemented mitigations; some requests may have experienced errors or higher latency. We're monitoring and will update within 60 minutes."

jordan-sre: Rolling shape to remaining nodes. I'm also toggling proxy keepalive tuning to reduce stream reconnects: `env PROXY_HTTP2_IDLE_TIMEOUT=30s` then reload.

ben-ml: Monitoring shows kv-cache regen rate stable. No signs of model regressions. Cost estimates if fallback kept at 30% for 1 hour: ~$1200.

kai (oncall): OK to proceed. Prioritize SLOs. Sam, ensure tickets open for AZ capacity request and follow-up with AWS.

sam-platform: Ticket AWS-123456 opened to request additional instance capacity in az1a; rep assigned but no firm ETA. Also filed infra runbook item to investigate qdisc defaults across images.

ops-bot: Update: error rate now 0.9% after 30m and shaping rollout complete. Traffic weight at 30% to eu-west1.

lia-cs: Sending external note now to impacted customers. Keeping high-touch list for customers with >5% error impact.

jordan-sre: Plan for next steps: 1) keep fallback in place until AWS confirms extra capacity or we see stable metrics for 60m 2) run deeper NIC firmware/drivers audit on az1a fleet 3) post-incident RCA to include kernel tx scheduling and retry behavior.

kai (oncall): Handoff to night shift: @jordan-sre you'll lead the follow-up monitoring and RCA, @sam-platform keep AWS ticket active, @lia-cs manage comms. I'm closing active pager now but will remain available.

ops-bot: Incident update: status=stabilized, severity=sev3, incident_id=INC-2765439999. Next update due in 60m or on status change.

ben-ml: Thanks team. Quick note — consider implementing regional pre-warming for ephemeral pools on cross-region tiers to reduce cold start pressure when shifting traffic next time.

lia-cs: Logged customers notified list and responses in ticket TKT-7890. No escalations so far.

kai (oncall): Good job. Handoff complete. Will add timeline to the incident doc and schedule RCA meeting tomorrow.

jordan-sre: Adding debugging artifacts to the incident doc: tcpdump snippets, `tc -s qdisc` outputs, kernel versions per host.

ops-bot: Incident closed for active paging. All follow-ups tracked in INC-2765439999.
